title: Weekly Unified Field research and verification

automation.task_title: Weekly Unified Field research and verification
consolidates: Weekly Unified Field research and verification
automation.note: The existing Friday Research Brief was updated in place; no duplicate scheduled task was created.

scope: Agentic AI, multi-agent orchestration, local/cloud AI integration, task queues, fault tolerance, self-healing, shared memory, and reproducible verification
Quantum/classical computing, compression, memory architectures, energy-efficient compute, and measured energy-per-successful-task performance
Privacy engineering, informed consent, data minimization, user sovereignty, accessibility, security, and human-centered design

Labor economics and worker bargaining power; algorithmic management and discrimination; surveillance; dark patterns; attention capture; exploitative data practices; effects on children and vulnerable communities
Computational biology, cancer research, scientific AI workflows, and reproducible biomedical analysis
Human-centered, life-preserving, non-extractive technology and relevant science, culture, and society
execution_requirements: Prioritize work published since the previous briefing; use a seven-day fallback if needed and verify dates and source links.

Prefer peer-reviewed primary studies, standards, official technical documentation, datasets, regulatory guidance, benchmark papers, authoritative institutional sources, and primary repository/release artifacts; label preprints.
For each significant finding, report research question, methods/evidence, main finding, practical implications, limitations, and material counterevidence.
Identify who benefits, who bears costs or risks, and measurable engineering requirements or safeguards relevant to Unified Field.

When authorized GitHub access exists, inspect current source, exact commit SHAs, PRs, issues, workflow runs, tests, and evidence files; independently inspect changed code rather than relying on builder summaries.
Evaluate fault detection/recovery, idempotency, concurrency, persistence, approval provenance, secret handling, privacy, retention, accessibility, security boundaries, and energy efficiency.
Distinguish implemented-and-tested capabilities from proposals, simulations, reported results, and unverified claims.
Recommend one or two high-value bounded experiments, prioritizing genuinely new tests; include measurable success criteria, safety boundaries, and reproducible verification paths.
Do not modify repositories, merge PRs, close issues, deploy services, run destructive operations, or change system settings.
Deliver a report every Friday even when there are no major developments; explicitly state when no meaningful new evidence was found.
Never invent results, benchmarks, citations, repository status, or test outcomes.
report_sections: Notable findings with source and publication date
Human impact: beneficiaries, cost-bearers, and risks
Unified Field project verification with exact repository evidence
One or two recommended next experiments
Direct source links and paywall labels

governance.approval_boundary: Research and recommendations only; no repository mutations or privileged actions.
governance.evidence_rule: A scheduled report, repository artifact, health endpoint, or green unit test alone does not establish end-to-end capability or societal impact.
governance.privacy_rule: Do not publish secrets, private conversation contents, tokens, personal records, or device credentials.

created_from: User-approved consolidation of the existing Friday Research Brief with the expanded Unified Field research and independent verification scope.
